description:
The extracted weight-loss table for the named drugs, joined to trial design, one row per arm and timepoint.

Rows are NOT collapsed to one number per drug. The corpus holds several doses, timepoints and
estimands per trial, and picking a single winner per drug would mean choosing between them
here, silently and on the caller's behalf. The comparison is theirs to make; this returns the
rows and the labels needed to make it correctly.

`estimand` takes a family ("treatment-policy" or "on-treatment") or one exact label. A family
returns every label in it, so asking for treatment-policy also returns the treatment-regimen
rows, which are the same reading under Lilly's name for it; `estimand_filter` in the response
says which it did and which labels it included.

`ci_lower` and `ci_upper` do not always bracket `value_pct`. On some rows the published interval
is of the estimated difference against the comparator, which is a smaller number: `ci_of` names
the key of the row the interval brackets, so row[row["ci_of"]] is the bracketed figure, and
`ci_against` says what the difference is against (placebo on most rows, dapagliflozin or
semaglutide at the matching dose on others). `ci_level_pct` is the confidence level, 95 except
where a paper reported 97% intervals. Quote an interval only with the figure `ci_of` names.
name: compare_efficacy
title: Compare weight-loss efficacy
